verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕又娶了一妻，名叫基土拉。
verses.en: Abraham had taken[NOTE:1] another[NOTE:2] wife, named Keturah.
notes: Or “took.”sn Abraham had taken another wife. These events are not necessarily in chronological order following the events of the preceding chapter. They are listed here to summarize Abraham’s other descendants before the narrative of his death.
Heb “And Abraham added and took.”

verses.zh: 基土拉给他生了心兰、约珊、米但、米甸、伊施巴，和书亚。
verses.en: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

verses.zh: 约珊生了示巴和底但。底但的子孙是亚书利族、利都是族，和利乌米族。
verses.en: Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan.[NOTE:1] The descendants of Dedan were the Asshurites, Letushites, and Leummites.
notes: The names Sheba and Dedan appear in Gen 10:7 as descendants of Ham through Cush and Raamah. Since these two names are usually interpreted to be place names, one plausible suggestion is that some of Abraham’s descendants lived in those regions and took names linked with it.

verses.zh: 米甸的儿子是以法、以弗、哈诺、亚比大，和以勒大。这都是基土拉的子孙。
verses.en: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were descendants[NOTE:1] of Keturah.
notes: Or “sons.”

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕将一切所有的都给了以撒。
verses.en: Everything he owned Abraham left to his son Isaac.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕把财物分给他庶出的众子，趁着自己还在世的时候打发他们离开他的儿子以撒，往东方去。
verses.en: But while he was still alive, Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines[NOTE:1] and sent them off to the east, away from his son Isaac.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the sons of the concubines who [belonged] to Abraham.”
Heb “And he sent them away from upon Isaac his son, while he was still living, eastward to the land of the east.”

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕一生的年日是一百七十五岁。
verses.en: Abraham lived a total of[NOTE:1] 175 years.
notes: Heb “and these are the days of the years of the lifetime of Abraham that he lived.” The normal genealogical formula is expanded here due to the importance of the life of Abraham.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕寿高年迈，气绝而死，归到他列祖（原文是本民）那里。
verses.en: Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man who had lived a full life.[NOTE:1] He joined his ancestors.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “old and full.”
Heb “And he was gathered to his people.” In the ancient Israelite view he joined his deceased ancestors in Sheol, the land of the dead.

verses.zh: 他两个儿子以撒、以实玛利把他埋葬在麦比拉洞里。这洞在幔利前、赫人琐辖的儿子以弗仑的田中，
verses.en: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah[NOTE:1] near Mamre, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar, the Hittite.[NOTE:2]
notes: The cave of Machpelah was the place Abraham had purchased as a burial place for his wife Sarah (Gen 23:17-18).
The Hebrew term “Hittite” derives from the name Heth; see the note at Gen 23:3.

verses.zh: 就是亚伯拉罕向赫人买的那块田。亚伯拉罕和他妻子撒拉都葬在那里。
verses.en: This was the field Abraham had purchased from the sons of Heth.[NOTE:1] There Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah.
notes: See the note on the phrase “sons of Heth” in Gen 23:3.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕死了以后，　神赐福给他的儿子以撒。以撒靠近庇耳・拉海・莱居住。
verses.en: After Abraham’s death, God blessed[NOTE:1] his son Isaac. Isaac lived near Beer Lahai Roi.[NOTE:2]
notes: God blessed Isaac. The Hebrew verb “bless” in this passage must include all the gifts that God granted to Isaac. But fertility was not one of them, at least not for 20 years, because Rebekah was barren as well (see v. 21).
Beer Lahai Roi. See the note on this place name in Gen 24:62.

verses.zh: 撒拉的使女埃及人夏甲给亚伯拉罕所生的儿子是以实玛利。
verses.en: This is the account of Abraham’s son Ishmael,[NOTE:1] whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.
notes: This is the account of Ishmael. The Book of Genesis tends to tidy up the family records at every turning point. Here, before proceeding with the story of Isaac’s family, the narrative traces Ishmael’s family line. Later, before discussing Jacob’s family, the narrative traces Esau’s family line (see Gen 36).

verses.zh: 以实玛利儿子们的名字，按着他们的家谱记在下面。以实玛利的长子是尼拜约，又有基达、亚德别、米比衫、
verses.en: These are the names of Ishmael’s sons, by their names according to their records:[NOTE:1] Nebaioth (Ishmael’s firstborn), Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
notes: The meaning of this line is not easily understood. The sons of Ishmael are listed here “by their names” and “according to their descendants.”

verses.zh: 米施玛、度玛、玛撒、
verses.en: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

verses.zh: 哈大、提玛、伊突、拿非施、基底玛。
verses.en: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

verses.zh: 这是以实玛利众子的名字，照着他们的村庄、营寨，作了十二族的族长。
verses.en: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names by their settlements and their camps—twelve princes[NOTE:1] according to their clans.
notes: Or “tribal chieftains.”

verses.zh: 以实玛利享寿一百三十七岁，气绝而死，归到他列祖（原文是本民）那里。
verses.en: Ishmael lived a total of[NOTE:1] 137 years. He breathed his last and died; then he joined his ancestors.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And these are the days of the years of Ishmael.”
Heb “And he was gathered to his people.” In the ancient Israelite view he joined his deceased ancestors in Sheol, the land of the dead.

verses.zh: 他子孙的住处在他众弟兄东边，从哈腓拉直到埃及前的书珥，正在亚述的道上。
verses.en: His descendants[NOTE:1] settled from Havilah to Shur, which runs next to[NOTE:2] Egypt all the way[NOTE:3] to Asshur.[NOTE:4] They settled[NOTE:5] away from all their relatives.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (Ishmael’s descendants) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “which is by the face of,” or near the border. The territory ran along the border of Egypt.
Heb “as you go.”
The name Asshur refers here to a tribal area in the Sinai.
Heb “he fell.”

Heb “upon the face of all his brothers.” This last expression, obviously alluding to the earlier oracle about Ishmael (Gen 16:12), could mean that the descendants of Ishmael lived in hostility to others or that they lived in a territory that was opposite the lands of their relatives. While there is some ambiguity about the meaning, the line probably does give a hint of the Ishmaelite-Israelite conflicts to come.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕的儿子以撒的后代记在下面。亚伯拉罕生以撒。
verses.en: This is the account of Isaac,[NOTE:1] the son of Abraham.Abraham became the father of Isaac.
notes: This is the account of Isaac. What follows for several chapters is not the account of Isaac, except briefly, but the account of Jacob and Esau. The next chapters tell what became of Isaac and his family.

verses.zh: 以撒娶利百加为妻的时候正四十岁。利百加是巴旦・亚兰地的亚兰人彼土利的女儿，是亚兰人拉班的妹子。
verses.en: When Isaac was forty years old, he married Rebekah,[NOTE:1] the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan Aram and sister of Laban the Aramean.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And Isaac was the son of forty years when he took Rebekah.”

Some valuable information is provided here. We learn here that Isaac married thirty-five years before Abraham died, that Rebekah was barren for 20 years, and that Abraham would have lived to see Jacob and Esau begin to grow up. The death of Abraham was recorded in the first part of the chapter as a “tidying up” of one generation before beginning the account of the next.

verses.zh: 以撒因他妻子不生育，就为她祈求耶和华；耶和华应允他的祈求，他的妻子利百加就怀了孕。
verses.en: Isaac prayed[NOTE:1] to the Lord on behalf of his wife because she was childless. The Lord answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
notes: The Hebrew verb עָתַר (ʿatar), translated “prayed” here, appears in the story of God’s judgment on Egypt in which Moses asked the Lord to remove the plagues. The cognate word in Arabic means “to slaughter for sacrifice,” and the word is used in Zeph 3:10 to describe worshipers who bring offerings. Perhaps some ritual accompanied Isaac’s prayer here.

verses.zh: 孩子们在她腹中彼此相争，她就说：「若是这样，我为甚么活着呢（或译：我为甚么如此呢）？」她就去求问耶和华。
verses.en: But the children struggled[NOTE:1] inside her, and she said, “Why is this happening to me?”[NOTE:2] So she asked the Lord,[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew word used here suggests a violent struggle that was out of the ordinary.
Heb “If [it is] so, why [am] I this [way]?” Rebekah wanted to know what was happening to her, but the question itself reflects a growing despair over the struggle of the unborn children.
Asked the Lord. In other passages (e.g., 1 Sam 9:9) this expression refers to inquiring of a prophet, but no details are provided here.

verses.zh: 耶和华对她说：两国在你腹内；两族要从你身上出来。这族必强于那族；将来大的要服事小的。
verses.en: and the Lord said to her,“Two nations[NOTE:1] are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from within you.One people will be stronger than the other,and the older will serve the younger.”
notes: By metonymy the two children in her womb are described as two nations of which the two children, Jacob and Esau, would become the fathers. The language suggests there would be a struggle between these nations, with one being stronger than the other. The oracle reveals that all of Jacob’s scheming was unnecessary in the final analysis. He would have become the dominant nation without using deception to steal his brother’s blessing.

verses.zh: 生产的日子到了，腹中果然是双子。
verses.en: When the time came for Rebekah to give birth,[NOTE:1] there were[NOTE:2] twins in her womb.
notes: Heb “And her days were filled to give birth.”
Heb “look!” By the use of the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”), the narrator invites the audience to view the scene as if they were actually present at the birth.

verses.zh: 先产的身体发红，浑身有毛，如同皮衣，他们就给他起名叫以扫（就是有毛的意思）。
verses.en: The first came out reddish[NOTE:1] all over,[NOTE:2] like a hairy[NOTE:3] garment, so they named him Esau.[NOTE:4]
notes: Reddish. The Hebrew word translated “reddish” is אַדְמוֹנִי (ʾadmoni), which forms a wordplay on the Edomites, Esau’s descendants. The writer sees in Esau’s appearance at birth a sign of what was to come. After all, the reader has already been made aware of the “nations” that were being born.
Heb “all of him.”

Hairy. Here is another wordplay involving the descendants of Esau. The Hebrew word translated “hairy” is שֵׂעָר (seʿar); the Edomites will later live in Mount Seir, perhaps named for its wooded nature.
Heb “And they called his name Esau.” The name “Esau” (עֵשָׂו, ʿesav) is not etymologically related to שֵׂעָר (seʿar), but it draws on some of the sounds.

verses.zh: 随后又生了以扫的兄弟，手抓住以扫的脚跟，因此给他起名叫雅各（就是抓住的意思）。利百加生下两个儿子的时候，以撒年正六十岁。
verses.en: When his brother came out with[NOTE:1] his hand clutching Esau’s heel, they named him Jacob.[NOTE:2] Isaac was sixty years old[NOTE:3] when they were born.
notes: The disjunctive clause describes an important circumstance accompanying the birth. Whereas Esau was passive at birth, Jacob was active.

The name Jacob is a play on the Hebrew word for “heel” (עָקֵב, ʿaqev). The name (since it is a verb) probably means something like “may he protect,” that is, as a rearguard, dogging the heels. It did not have a negative connotation until Esau redefined it. This name was probably chosen because of the immediate association with the incident of grabbing the heel. After receiving such an oracle, the parents would have preserved in memory almost every detail of the unusual births.tn Heb “And he called his name Jacob.” Some ancient witnesses read “they called his name Jacob” (see v. 25). In either case the subject is indefinite.
Heb “the son of sixty years.”

verses.zh: 两个孩子渐渐长大，以扫善于打猎，常在田野；雅各为人安静，常住在帐棚里。
verses.en: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skilled[NOTE:1] hunter, a man of the open fields, but Jacob was an even-tempered man, living in tents.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “knowing.”

The disjunctive clause juxtaposes Jacob with Esau and draws attention to the striking contrasts. In contrast to Esau, a man of the field, Jacob was civilized, as the phrase “living in tents” signifies. Whereas Esau was a skillful hunter, Jacob was calm and even-tempered (תָּם, tam), which normally has the idea of “blameless.”

verses.zh: 以撒爱以扫，因为常吃他的野味；利百加却爱雅各。
verses.en: Isaac loved Esau because he had a taste for fresh game,[NOTE:1] but Rebekah loved[NOTE:2] Jacob.
notes: Heb “the taste of game was in his mouth.” The word for “game,” “venison” is here the same Hebrew word as “hunter” in the last verse. Here it is a metonymy, referring to that which the hunter kills.
The disjunctive clause juxtaposes Rebekah with Jacob and draws attention to the contrast. The verb here is a participle, drawing attention to Rebekah’s continuing, enduring love for her son.

verses.zh: 有一天，雅各熬汤，以扫从田野回来累昏了。
verses.en: Now Jacob cooked some stew,[NOTE:1] and when Esau came in from the open fields, he was famished.
notes: Jacob cooked some stew. There are some significant words and wordplays in this story that help clarify the points of the story. The verb “cook” is זִיד (zid), which sounds like the word for “hunter” (צַיִד, tsayid). This is deliberate, for the hunter becomes the hunted in this story. The word זִיד means “to cook, to boil,” but by the sound play with צַיִד it comes to mean “set a trap by cooking.” The usage of the word shows that it can also have the connotation of acting presumptuously (as in boiling over). This too may be a comment on the scene. For further discussion of the rhetorical devices in the Jacob narratives, see J. P. Fokkelman, Narrative Art in Genesis (SSN).

verses.zh: 以扫对雅各说：「我累昏了，求你把这红汤给我喝。」因此以扫又叫以东（就是红的意思）。
verses.en: So Esau said to Jacob, “Feed[NOTE:1] me some of the red stuff—yes, this red stuff—because I’m starving!” (That is why he was also called[NOTE:2] Edom.)[NOTE:3]
notes: The rare term לָעַט (laʿat), translated “feed,” is used in later Hebrew for feeding animals (see Jastrow, 714). If this nuance was attached to the word in the biblical period, then it may depict Esau in a negative light, comparing him to a hungry animal. Famished Esau comes in from the hunt, only to enter the trap. He can only point at the red stew and ask Jacob to feed him.
The verb has no expressed subject and so is given a passive translation.

Esau’s descendants would eventually be called Edom. Edom was the place where they lived, so-named probably because of the reddish nature of the hills. The writer can use the word “red” to describe the stew that Esau gasped for to convey the nature of Esau and his descendants. They were a lusty, passionate, and profane people who lived for the moment. Again, the wordplay is meant to capture the “omen in the nomen.”

verses.zh: 雅各说：「你今日把长子的名分卖给我吧。」
verses.en: But Jacob replied, “First[NOTE:1] sell me your birthright.”
notes: Heb “today.”

verses.zh: 以扫说：「我将要死，这长子的名分于我有甚么益处呢？」
verses.en: “Look,” said Esau, “I’m about to die! What use is the birthright to me?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And what is this to me, a birthright?”

verses.zh: 雅各说：「你今日对我起誓吧。」以扫就对他起了誓，把长子的名分卖给雅各。
verses.en: But Jacob said, “Swear an oath to me now.”[NOTE:1] So Esau[NOTE:2] swore an oath to him and sold his birthright[NOTE:3] to Jacob.
notes: Heb “Swear to me today.”
Heb “and he”; the referent (Esau) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

And sold his birthright. There is evidence from Hurrian culture that rights of inheritance were occasionally sold or transferred. Here Esau is portrayed as a profane person who would at the moment rather have a meal than the right to inherit. He will soon forget this trade and seek his father’s blessing in spite of it.

verses.zh: 于是雅各将饼和红豆汤给了以扫，以扫吃了喝了，便起来走了。这就是以扫轻看了他长子的名分。
verses.en: Then Jacob gave Esau some bread and lentil stew; Esau ate and drank, then got up and went out.[NOTE:1] So Esau despised his birthright.[NOTE:2]
notes: The style here is typical of Hebrew narrative; after the tension is resolved with the dialogue, the working out of it is recorded in a rapid sequence of verbs (“gave”; “ate”; “drank”; “got up”; “went out”). See also Gen 3:1-7 for another example.

So Esau despised his birthright. This clause, which concludes the episode, is a summary statement which reveals the underlying significance of Esau’s actions. “To despise” means to treat something as worthless or with contempt. Esau’s willingness to sell his birthright was evidence that he considered it to be unimportant.
